Hi Alice — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Call recap / goals:
- Objective: 2-week POC to validate latency, throughput and cost for Acme’s customer-facing summarization flow (approx. 600–800 concurrent users during peak).
- Success criteria (proposed):
  - 95th percentile token latency <= 400ms for 512-token requests under target load
  - End-to-end throughput to support 800 concurrent users with <5% error rate
  - Cost per 1k requests within the target budget (you proposed $X–$Y)
  - Model quality: summaries meet QA pass rate >= 90% on your eval set

POC plan / timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize SOW & infra checklist; sign DocuSign
- Week 1 (kickoff): reserved capacity provisioned, test dataset ingest, baseline runs
- Week 2: full-load run, tuning (batching, KV cache), quality evals, final report

Ownership:
- Commercial / timeline: Marissa Cole (me)
- Technical / infra & tuning: Aditya Rao (SE)
- Customer success / onboarding & eval coordination: Lauren Bishop

Capacity questions we need to confirm from our side: reserved GPU type/count, autoscaling headroom, expected burst profile. Aditya — can you propose a capacity plan (reserved + autoscale + burst) and an estimate attachment we can share with Acme?

Attachments: poc-sow.pdf (draft SOW), infra-checklist.xlsx

Next steps for Alice / Acme:
- Confirm success criteria above (or propose edits)
- Confirm kickoff week (we recommended starting the week of Feb 22)
- Provide a small eval dataset (redacted) and a list of internal contacts (who will run quality checks)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Aditya’s capacity plan and an updated SOW/DocuSign link early next week.

Hi Alice / team — following Marissa’s recap, here’s a proposed capacity plan and notes on autoscaling / burst behavior for the POC. I attached a CSV with estimates.

Recommended reserved capacity:
- 2 x NVIDIA A100-40GB (reserved for baseline load). This gives predictable latency for steady-state requests and isolates your traffic for the POC.

Autoscaling and burst:
- Autoscale policy: scale up from reserved capacity to up to 6 instances (same SKU) based on sustained queue / 95th latency breach for >30s.
- Burst behavior: short bursts (up to 10 instances) allowed for 2–5 minutes to absorb traffic spikes; bursts are limited by per-customer pool quota. Bursts incur incremental usage charges.

Performance & tuning notes:
- Use sequence-length-aware batching (we’ll recommend batch windows and token caps) to maximize throughput while targeting the latency SLO.
- Enable prefix (KV) caching for repeated contexts (summary templates) — should reduce per-token compute significantly.
- For evaluation, provide a representative sample (1000 requests with distribution) so we can simulate expected load.

Operational dependencies / network notes:
- For Private/Dedicated POCs, we’ll need VPC peering or a secure tunnel and an IP allowlist; please confirm networking window with your infra team.
- If you require KMS/HSM for key control, share the KMS endpoint details early so we can provision access.

Estimate (attachment): capacity-estimate.csv — includes estimated RPS, GPU utilization, and expected incremental cost for autoscale/burst.

If you’d like a cheaper baseline for purely functional testing, we can spin up one lower-cost 8GB-quantized instance, but that won’t meet the latency SLO under concurrency.

I’m happy to run a short load-test with Acme’s sample set once we have the reserved capacity provisioned.

—

1) Can we increase reserved capacity mid-POC if we find baseline is undersized? How fast is that turnaround?
2) For burst beyond autoscale limits (e.g., black friday-type spikes), what’s graceful degradation behavior? Do you failover to a smaller model or queue requests?
3) Data retention & logs: we need confirmation that logs for POC runs can be retained for 90 days and that we can get token-level cost breakdowns for each test run.

Personnel/ownership on our side: I’ll own coordination and evaluation — I’m looping in Bob Chen (bchen@fintech.io) who will run QA on the summaries.

Proposed kickoff bump: can we start the week of Feb 22 instead of Mar 1? We can free up infra time this week to provide sample data and confirm networking.

If you can confirm answers to the 3 items above and send a DocuSign link for the SOW, we can sign and get things moving.

Alice — great questions. Quick answers + confirmed next steps: 

1) Increasing reserved capacity mid-POC: yes — we can increase reserved GPUs. Typical provisioning time is 24–48 hours for capacity changes in Dedicated pools; we’ll prioritize requests for active POCs. Aditya will own the provisioning request and keep you posted.

2) Burst and graceful degradation: we’ll autoscale to the configured max (6) and allow short bursts to 10 instances for 2–5 minutes. If traffic exceeds burst limits we support these graceful behaviors (in order):
  - Queue short requests (configurable queue timeout)
  - Route to a lower-cost/quantized model variant if you opt-in (we’ll flag any quality regression)
  - Return 429s when capacity is exhausted (we’ll monitor and alert)

3) Data retention & logs: we can retain logs for 90 days for the POC and provide token-level cost breakdowns per test run. We’ll include the cost/latency dashboard link in the final POC report.

Action items / next steps:
- Marissa: update SOW with kickoff week Feb 22 and send DocuSign link (attached).
- Aditya: submit reserved GPU provisioning (2 x A100-40GB baseline) and schedule an initial load-test the morning of Feb 23.
- Lauren: send onboarding checklist and coordinate QA alignment with Bob.
- Alice / Acme: sign SOW via DocuSign; share sample eval dataset and networking contact.
